findings.title: Topic unsubscribe changes state on an unauthenticated GET
findings.body: TopicsController#unsubscribe is routed only as GET (config/routes.rb) and immediately writes TopicUser.notification_level. Rails CSRF protection does not cover GET, and the link embedded in notification emails carries no per-recipient token. Any page that can make the browser request that URL while the victim is logged in (an img or link on another site, a link previewer in the same browser) will change that user's notification level using their session cookie. The link is also not bound to the mailbox recipient, so on a shared browser it mutates whichever account happens to be logged in, not the person who was emailed. Because the transition is not idempotent (watching/tracking becomes regular, a second fetch then mutes), a refresh or a second request does not even settle on the same level.

findings.title: Unsubscribe 500s when the user has no TopicUser row
findings.body: unsubscribe does TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id]) and then reads tu.notification_level with no nil check. TopicView succeeding only means the user can see the topic; it does not create a topic_users row. Any logged-in user who opens /t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe for a topic they have never visited (or whose row was removed) gets NoMethodError instead of being muted. That URL is publicly linked from email and is not restricted to people who already have a TopicUser.

findings.title: Watching and tracking users are not actually unsubscribed
findings.body: If notification_level is above regular (tracking=2 or watching=3), the action sets regular (1); only regular or muted users are set to muted. Regular still emails replies, mentions, and quotes, and watching is exactly the level that emails every new post. The email copy in server.en.yml tells the recipient this link will "stop receiving notifications about this particular topic", and the confirmation string in client.en.yml always says they will stop receiving notifications. After one click a watcher is only demoted to regular, so those emails continue, and the confirmation is false. A second request (refresh, or the non-idempotent GET being fetched twice) then takes the else branch and mutes, so the end state depends on how many times the URL was hit.

findings.title: Direct save skips notifications_reason_id so auto-track can undo the change
findings.body: The new level is written with tu.notification_level= and tu.save! instead of TopicUser.change. change is what sets notifications_changed_at, notifications_reason_id (user_changed), and the MessageBus notification_level_change event. update_last_read in topic_user.rb promotes notification_level back to tracking whenever notifications_reason_id is still null and time-on-topic exceeds the auto-track threshold. Users who were at the default regular level (reason id null) and get muted here will be bumped back to tracking the next time post timings are recorded, so the unsubscribe does not stick. Other open tabs also never hear about the change.

findings.title: Unsubscribe template path does not match the Ember route
findings.body: The route is registered as top-level topicUnsubscribe (app-route-map.js.es6), and the controller and view are named topic-unsubscribe, so Ember looks up the template topic-unsubscribe. This file lives at templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs, which compiles to the template name topic/unsubscribe used only by a nested topic.unsubscribe route. Nothing in the route calls renderTemplate to point at that name. After the server action runs, the Ember app transitions to topicUnsubscribe and renders a missing template: the confirmation text and the topic-notifications-button never appear, so the user gets a blank page and cannot correct the level the GET just wrote.

findings.title: No spec covers the unsubscribe action or the new email link
findings.body: The only test change is in spec/components/email/message_builder_spec.rb, which passes unsubscribe_url: "/t/1234/unsubscribe" so I18n interpolation of the rewritten unsubscribe_link string does not raise. It never asserts that the per-topic sentence or URL is actually in the body. There is no controller or mailer spec for TopicsController#unsubscribe: missing TopicUser, watching versus regular, slug redirect, or that notification emails include topic.unsubscribe_url. The non-idempotent level change and the nil crash can ship unnoticed.
